html:
Remark. Provenance of the recursive atom-knot atlas entries

Provenance of the atlas entries

Every entry is computed from a single reproducible chain of sources, so the table never drifts from the witnesses it summarizes. The atlas is auto-rendered by recursive_atom_knot_atlas_render.py.

Sources of truth (in order):

  1. confined-particle.md — GB-NF particle registry (canonical T_w).
  2. mass-table-ppb.witness.json — D..{}^{40}Ca (manual-historical, recursive, magic-A).
  3. methodology-deprecation.witness.json — per-particle methodology record.
  4. hp_volume.py — \geq 50-digit symbolic-q Markov-closure \to \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}.
  5. y_lambda_wenzl_bridge_extended.py — symbolic-q Wenzl bridge for y_\lambda.

These compose in that order: the particle registry fixes the canonical T_w, the mass-table witness supplies the tabulated masses, the methodology record tags each particle's derivation method, hp_volume.py supplies \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}, and the Wenzl bridge supplies y_\lambda.

For principled-derivation entries (electron, proton, neutron) the hyperbolic volume of the Markov closure is computed from the \sigma-braid word at \geq 50 decimal digits via hp_volume_of_link_closure(braid_word, digits=50) which calls SnapPy's Link(braid_closure=...).exterior.high_precision inside mpmath.workdps(50). When any input changes, witness_staleness_tracker.py marks the affected entries stale and the atlas is recomputed from the sources above; no entry is maintained by hand.
